title: Systemic sclerosis (CREST): esophageal dysmotility from fibrous replacement of the muscularis
vignette: A 35-year-old woman comes to the clinic due to severe heartburn that is resistant to over-the-counter antacids. The patient has no known medical problems and takes no other medications. She occasionally has a glass of wine with dinner but does not use tobacco or illicit drugs. Physical examination shows scattered telangiectasias on the face, several ulcers at the tips of the fingers, and small calcium deposits in the soft tissues of the hands and elbows. Which of the following processes is the most likely cause of this patient's heartburn?

clues.text: severe heartburn that is resistant to over-the-counter antacids
clues.note: Refractory reflux in a young woman with skin findings suggests a motility problem (esophageal dysmotility), not simple acid excess.
Telangiectasias are the 'T' of CREST (limited systemic sclerosis).

clues.text: several ulcers at the tips of the fingers
clues.note: Digital tip ulcers reflect Raynaud phenomenon and sclerodactyly-related ischemia in systemic sclerosis.

clues.text: small calcium deposits in the soft tissues of the hands and elbows
clues.note: Calcinosis cutis is the 'C' of CREST - subcutaneous calcium deposits.

whatMatters: Telangiectasias + digital ulcers + calcinosis = CREST (limited systemic sclerosis). It causes ESOPHAGEAL DYSMOTILITY: atrophy and FIBROUS REPLACEMENT of the smooth muscle (muscularis) of the lower esophagus, making the body and lower esophageal sphincter atonic -> reflux and refractory heartburn. Answer B.
strategy: Recognize CREST (Calcinosis, Raynaud, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasia) and link the heartburn to its esophageal mechanism: fibrosis of the lower esophageal smooth muscle -> weak/atonic LES and body -> GERD. Reject a sliding hiatal hernia (abnormal GE junction location - not the sclerosis mechanism), increased acid production (Zollinger-Ellison/gastrinoma), increased LES tone (that would impair opening, as in achalasia - opposite of reflux), and diffuse esophageal spasm (uncoordinated contractions - dysphagia/chest pain, not this fibrotic atony).

options.text: Abnormal location of the gastroesophageal junction
Fibrous replacement of the muscularis in the lower esophagus
Increase in resting lower esophageal sphincter tone
Uncoordinated, simultaneous muscle contractions in the lower esophagus

eliminations.label: Abnormal GE junction location - hiatal hernia
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a sliding hiatal hernia (herniation of the GE junction/stomach through the hiatus). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it can cause reflux but does not explain this patient's CREST features; her reflux is from esophageal smooth-muscle fibrosis. ✅ Correct if: reflux from a hiatal hernia without systemic sclerosis.

eliminations.label: Increased gastric acid - gastrinoma
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: acid hypersecretion (e.g., Zollinger-Ellison/gastrinoma). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: gastrinomas cause refractory peptic ulcers, and there's no such clue; her problem is impaired esophageal clearance/LES tone from sclerosis. ✅ Correct if: multiple refractory ulcers with high gastrin.

eliminations.label: Increased LES tone - achalasia (opposite)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a hypertonic lower esophageal sphincter that fails to relax (achalasia). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: increased LES tone causes DYSPHAGIA and food retention, not reflux; systemic sclerosis DECREASES LES tone. ✅ Correct if: achalasia (failure of LES relaxation, bird-beak esophagus).

eliminations.label: Uncoordinated simultaneous contractions - diffuse esophageal spasm
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: diffuse esophageal spasm (periodic, uncoordinated contractions from impaired inhibitory innervation). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it causes dysphagia and chest pain (corkscrew esophagus), not the atonic reflux of scleroderma. ✅ Correct if: intermittent dysphagia/chest pain with simultaneous contractions.

reasoning: Telangiectasias + digital ulcers + calcinosis = CREST (limited systemic sclerosis)
Systemic sclerosis causes esophageal dysmotility via smooth-muscle atrophy and fibrosis
The lower esophageal body and sphincter become atonic/dilated -> gastroesophageal reflux
-> fibrous replacement of the lower esophageal muscularis; answer B
mechanism: This patient has CREST syndrome - a LIMITED variant of SYSTEMIC SCLEROSIS defined by Calcinosis, Raynaud phenomenon, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, and Telangiectasia. Systemic sclerosis involves chronic autoimmune inflammation, vascular endothelial injury, and excessive fibroblast activation causing progressive tissue FIBROSIS. In the esophagus, the smooth muscle of the lower two-thirds undergoes ATROPHY and FIBROUS REPLACEMENT of the muscularis; the esophageal body and the LOWER ESOPHAGEAL SPHINCTER become atonic and dilated, reducing peristaltic clearance and lowering LES pressure. The result is GASTROESOPHAGEAL REFLUX with symptoms of heartburn, regurgitation, and dysphagia (and increased risk of Barrett esophagus and stricture). This mechanism explains the refractory heartburn. The distractors describe other esophageal problems: hiatal hernia (GE junction displacement), gastrinoma (acid hypersecretion), achalasia (increased LES tone/failed relaxation), and diffuse esophageal spasm (uncoordinated contractions) - none fit the scleroderma-related fibrotic atony.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Rheum/GI > systemic sclerosis (CREST): anticentromere antibody (limited), diffuse = anti-Scl-70; esophageal dysmotility from smooth-muscle atrophy/fibrosis -> low LES tone, GERD, Barrett, stricture.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: CREST -> esophageal smooth-muscle fibrosis -> atonic LES -> reflux/heartburn.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on CREST, systemic sclerosis, esophageal dysmotility, lower esophageal sphincter, or calcinosis/sclerodactyly? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Hiatal hernia = GE junction displacement; gastrinoma = acid excess; achalasia = HIGH LES tone; DES = uncoordinated contractions.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: scleroderma esophagus = fibrous replacement of smooth muscle -> hypotonic LES -> GERD (Barrett/stricture risk).

keywords.back: Calcinosis, Raynaud, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasia
Smooth-muscle atrophy + fibrous replacement -> atonic LES -> GERD
Increased tone / failure to relax (dysphagia, not reflux)

firstAid.detail: Rheum: esophageal smooth-muscle fibrosis -> hypotonic LES -> reflux.
GI > achalasia (high LES), DES (uncoordinated), hiatal hernia.

memoryHook: CREST scars the esophagus's muscle into stiff fibrous tissue - the lower sphincter goes limp, so acid climbs back up and antacids can't keep up.
